patients.label: 72-year-old woman with HSV-2 encephalitis presenting with chorea and mental status changes

identity_evidence.quote: A 72-year-old woman with a history of gastritis and urinary incontinence

attribution_limitations: An initial urinalysis was positive for leukocyte esterase, bacteria and white blood cells, while a later sentence among the work-up reported after the lumbar puncture states that urinalysis did not reveal any signs of infection. The source does not say whether the second is a repeat test or when it was done, and does not identify the two as the same test, so they are kept as separate observations without ordering and not treated as a source conflict.

Whether concurrent CNS autoimmunity contributed to the chorea is unresolved: it was suspected on hospital day six, and the authors conclude only a possible autoimmune cause of chorea can be diagnosed, since serum neuronal autoantibody testing was omitted. No confirmed autoimmune diagnosis is inferred.

limitations: No figures, tables or supplements are listed in the source.
No timing is given for the lumbar puncture, CSF results, urine studies or other workup relative to hospital day; none is inferred.
The source states there is no EEG data or brain biopsy; these are recorded only as an absence of data in the discussion, not as items.
Discussion statements about latent reactivation and mechanisms are hedged author interpretation and are not extracted as facts.

claims.text: A 72-year-old woman with a history of gastritis and urinary incontinence presented with depressed level of consciousness after one day of confusion and lethargy. She had a fever of 38.6°C without meningismus, psychomotor slowing, impaired attention and clearly visible choreiform movements of the neck and left upper extremity that she could not suppress. Initial tests showed mildly elevated C-reactive protein and an abnormal urinalysis.
